result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B's cost-at-cap math is more thorough: it includes AI search and payment fees, and almost all of it checks out, though the annual Family margin is off (about 35%, not 28%). It also frames its prices as unvalidated and proposes a paid pilot to test them. A has clean storage arithmetic and storage allowances with more room, but it leaves search out of its margins, makes vague claims about competitors and cold-tier savings, and doesn't frame its prices as things to test. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A's arithmetic is correct and complete. For each plan it adds storage, AI search and payment fees, and its Pro price clears the $60/mo storage cost at 5 TB with real margin; the only slip is the Family annual margin (about 35%, not 28%). A also explicitly frames its prices as unvalidated and proposes a pilot to test them. B has a useful tier ladder and flags costs A skips, such as app store fees and download bandwidth, but its margin figures leave out search cost, it makes vague claims about competitors and cold-storage savings, and it doesn't present its prices as starting points to test.
